title: Elements/DOM inspector
learningObjectives: Explain elements/dom inspector and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: The Elements or DOM inspector shows the live document tree and lets developers inspect, edit, and diagnose element structure. It can reveal generated nodes, attributes, accessibility information, and layout relationships.
understand.whyItMatters: Inspecting the live DOM helps distinguish the source HTML from the actual document after scripts have modified it.
understand.analogy: The DOM inspector is an X-ray view of the page structure currently in the browser.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: The console snippet inspects the live DOM; the Elements panel provides a visual tree and editing tools.

examples.explanation: The console snippet inspects the live DOM; the Elements panel provides a visual tree and editing tools.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the workflow or developer-tool concept; command examples require a practice repository.

practise.guidedTask: Inspect a page in developer tools. Find the main landmark, a nested button, and the element's ancestors.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
hints: Inspect actual files and browser behaviour.
Do not commit secrets or personal data.
Verify provider-specific deployment values before changing DNS.
